list.name: node
list.label: node
list.description: Training node (Ray NodeAddress). GPU indices repeat across nodes, so pick one.

list.name: gpu
list.label: gpu
list.description: Which GPUs get their own utilization-by-phase panel.

panels.title: Per-GPU phase (one lane per GPU x role)
panels.description: What each GPU is doing right now and over time. Lanes are (node, gpu, role): in colocated runs the same GPU has a rollout lane (gen/sleep, emitted by the vLLM server) and a trainer lane (logprob/update/weight-sync, emitted by the worker). idle = waiting for work / data.

targets.expr: (ray_verl_gpu_phase{role!="rollout"} unless on (gpu, NodeAddress) (ray_verl_gpu_phase{role="rollout"} == 1)) or (ray_verl_gpu_phase{role!="rollout"} * 0 and on (gpu, NodeAddress) (ray_verl_gpu_phase{role="rollout"} == 1))

panels.title: GPU utilization (%)
panels.description: Ray's per-GPU utilization (NVML), sampled every few seconds. GpuIndex matches the gpu tag of the phase lanes above.

panels.title: GPU memory used (%)
panels.description: Per-GPU VRAM in use (Ray gram metrics).

panels.title: GPU $gpu · utilization by phase
panels.description:
One panel per GPU (repeats over the $gpu variable). The utilization line is split into one series per phase -- each query returns the utilization samples only while that GPU is in that phase -- so the line changes color as the GPU moves through gen / logprob / update / weight-sync. Colors match the phase timeline at the top.

A GPU's two lanes are collapsed into one 'effective' phase: whichever lane is doing real work wins (rollout gen beats trainer idle; trainer update beats rollout sleep). If every lane is idle or sleeping, the GPU shows idle/sleep.
